answer: Require every agent to lock a stake that only matures slowly, like a glacier carving a terrace above the wharf: identity becomes expensive to duplicate because each copy must post real collateral and build a history of useful work before it can trade. A sybil operator can spin up a thousand names, but each needs its own bonded stake and its own time in the queue, so the cost of flooding the market scales linearly while the payoff stays flat, and fakes bleed money before they ever earn a reputation.
